answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing escrowed tasks that are later checked by randomly assigned, stake-bearing peers; a disputed result triggers review, and dishonest reviewers can lose their stake. Creating many fake identities does not multiply influence, because each task requires real work and each review risks bonded funds. A sybil attacker must therefore pay repeatedly in labor, capital, and possible slashing. The raven, spiral, and meadow labels can name task batches, but carry no weight in the trust calculation.
